segments.title: Washington Treaty subjects in the series
segments.summary: The Washington Treaty schedule covers capital ships, aircraft carriers, other vessel categories, fortifications, a treaty-cruiser design exercise, and a concluding review of the settlement.
segments.body: The Washington Treaty portion begins with the capital-ship and aircraft-carrier episodes, both already available when this outline was recorded. An installment on other ships and fortifications was scheduled for 2 June, followed on 3 June by an Ultimate Admiral: Dreadnoughts exercise to design a cruiser within the treaty framework. The 4 June episode would then review the overall equitable settlement. Together, these installments move from treaty limits on specific categories to the design choices those limits create.

evidence.note: The transcript lists the Washington Treaty capital-ship, carrier, other-ships, fortifications, and cruiser-design installments.

segments.title: London Treaty subjects and fleet categories
segments.summary: The London Treaty schedule moves through capital ships, carriers, the Pensacola class, possible cruiser designs, destroyers, sloops, other vessels, fortifications, and a concluding equitable settlement.
segments.body: The London Treaty portion was scheduled to begin with capital ships on 5 June and aircraft carriers on 6 June. A Pensacola-class episode on 7 June would open a separate series on US cruisers, followed on 8 June by an examination of what London Treaty cruisers might have looked like. Destroyers were planned for 9 June, followed by a possible Ultimate Admiral: Dreadnoughts battle among capital ships, cruisers, destroyers, or a mixed force. Sloops and other ships would follow on 11 June, fortifications on 12 June, and the final equitable-treaty overview on 13 June. The schedule connects limits across the fleet with a historical design example and counterfactual design or combat exercises.

evidence.note: The transcript enumerates the London Treaty installments and the fleet categories each will cover.
